title: nuc-seq/SNES
reason: scope:nuc-seq: The card and image target the DNA method nuc-seq, named Nuc-Seq in Wang et al. The depicted G2/M selection, lysis and time-limited Phi29 MDA core is supported by that full text. The Synthesis panel is a local elaboration of the same MDA, not an additional target method. op_s1 remains an unassigned grouped-schematic operation because its use in this implementation is not established by the inspected primary evidence. Thus unresolved applicability is confined to that terminal operation, not the G2/M/MDA architecture. The paper supports downstream whole-genome and optional exome sequencing, which are outside the drawn endpoint. The candidate RNA collection page has a different heading and an RNA→cDNA→tagmentation target and is excluded. Div-Seq is mentioned only in catalogue prose and is not a target of this figure.; scope:SNES: SNES means single nucleus exome sequencing, as the figure caption and Leung et al. title state; the card’s expansion single nucleotide exome sequencing is not used as a separate method. The SNES paper explicitly supports G2/M as well as G1/0 nuclei, so the drawn G2/M-selected input history and downstream lysis/MDA instances apply to its G2/M implementation. The unshown G1/0 alternative is not added to this graph or assigned this fixed G2/M input state. The depicted S1 step remains a grouped-schematic operation with unresolved SNES applicability: the inspected full text instead describes sonication and TA library construction after WGA and reports no S1 step. SNES’s defining exome capture is downstream context, not a depicted branch. This supported shared core does not establish identical complete experimental implementations of SNES and nuc-seq.

candidate.title: nuc-seq/SNES
candidate.scope: The supplied Illumina nuc-seq/SNES genomic-DNA schematic: the G2/M-selected single-nucleus route through lysis, limited Phi29 MDA, further branched synthesis and the depicted S1 nuclease-to-DNA endpoint, including the two excluded sorting candidates. nuc-seq and SNES are distinct grouped targets, not aliases; the shared G2/M/MDA core is paper-supported, while S1 member applicability is retained as unresolved at the grouped schematic level. This is an amplification architecture, not a complete executable protocol or adapter-library diagram. Downstream whole-genome versus exome readout is explained from the respective full texts without adding unshown preparation, capture or sequencing nodes. The unrelated RNA Nuc-Seq catalogue page and prose-only Div-Seq variation do not expand scope.

research_questions.question: The card and image target the DNA method nuc-seq, named Nuc-Seq in Wang et al. The depicted G2/M selection, lysis and time-limited Phi29 MDA core is supported by that full text. The Synthesis panel is a local elaboration of the same MDA, not an additional target method. op_s1 remains an unassigned grouped-schematic operation because its use in this implementation is not established by the inspected primary evidence. Thus unresolved applicability is confined to that terminal operation, not the G2/M/MDA architecture. The paper supports downstream whole-genome and optional exome sequencing, which are outside the drawn endpoint. The candidate RNA collection page has a different heading and an RNA→cDNA→tagmentation target and is excluded. Div-Seq is mentioned only in catalogue prose and is not a target of this figure.

SNES means single nucleus exome sequencing, as the figure caption and Leung et al. title state; the card’s expansion single nucleotide exome sequencing is not used as a separate method. The SNES paper explicitly supports G2/M as well as G1/0 nuclei, so the drawn G2/M-selected input history and downstream lysis/MDA instances apply to its G2/M implementation. The unshown G1/0 alternative is not added to this graph or assigned this fixed G2/M input state. The depicted S1 step remains a grouped-schematic operation with unresolved SNES applicability: the inspected full text instead describes sonication and TA library construction after WGA and reports no S1 step. SNES’s defining exome capture is downstream context, not a depicted branch. This supported shared core does not establish identical complete experimental implementations of SNES and nuc-seq.
